svg.title: obj.x : the data descriptor wins before the instance dict is read
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “obj.x : the data descriptor wins before the instance dict is read” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. A flowchart of Python attribute lookup: walk the MRO, and if the name is a data descriptor with __set__ call its __get__ immediately, otherwise check the instance dict, then non-data descriptors, then plain class attributes, then __getattr__. A recursive @property is crossed out in red as a RecursionError. Beside it the three method kinds and what each receives, a diamond inheritance graph with its C3 order D B C A object, and bars showing attribute reads at 4.6, 4.4, 12.8 and 49.6 nanoseconds.
